memory_candidates.content: In BimodalLogic, scripts/check-module-invariants.sh's --no-build flag (RUN_BUILD=0) skips exactly the checks that shell out to `lake env lean`/`lake build`/`lake exe` (C1, C2, C6's compile-check half, C14's #print-axioms half, C16, C24, C25, C36b) while leaving every content/structural check running (C3-C5, C7-C9, C11, C15, C36a, INV, etc.) unaffected. This makes `bash scripts/check-module-invariants.sh --no-build` a genuinely safe lightweight check under host memory pressure that forbids a `lake build`-class command.

When a mechanical gate (e.g. check-module-invariants.sh's INV check, or typst-sync-check.sh) fails after a multi-phase dispatch, and the failure's two named files were last hand-edited by a PRIOR task's commit, do not assume the failure is pre-existing from that git-log fact alone: git log on a file shows when its CONTENT was last edited, not when it went stale relative to a live regeneration that depends on OTHER files elsewhere in the tree (e.g. a generated line-count table over a whole subtree). To actually root-cause which commit introduced the staleness, use disposable `git worktree add --detach <path> <commit>` checkouts (non-destructive to the working tree) and re-run the gate's read-only check mode at several candidate commits via bisection. In this case the INV check passed clean through the task's own plan-creation commit (no Lean files touched) and first failed at the task's own Phase-1 implementation commit, proving the task's own edits -- not a prior task's -- caused the drift. The fix was then a pure mechanical regeneration (the gate's own --emit-inventory writer mode), declared as a scope-extension in the summary, exactly analogous to the already-sanctioned typst/generated/status.typ regeneration pattern.
